solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pastry served in Mostar, tasty

indicators.note: the letters wanted are served up inside the run of words Mostar, tasty, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A food review: something sweet served in the Bosnian city of Mostar was tasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' signals the answer sits inside 'MosTAR Tasty'.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pie of pastry with a sweet filling is a standard example of a pastry dish.

clue.text: Wrong lock of hair Dad's cut

indicators.note: Dad's has cut the lock of hair, so it is inserted into it

parts.note: a tress is a long lock of hair
Pa is Dad, so Pa's gives PAS

explanation.surface: A father wrongly snipping off a lock of a child's hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad's' is read as 'Dad has', the subject of 'cut'; 'Wrong' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to sin or do wrong is an old sense, as in the Lord's Prayer.

clue.text: Divulge private information about ration one spurned

indicators.note: one is spurned, rejected and taken out of the word ration

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone leaks private details about their own ration, which another person spurned.
explanation.definitionFit: To inform on someone is to betray their secrets, an informal phrasal verb.

clue.text: Clown getting a pet for pounds in capital

indicators.note: the clown gets a new piece in place of one letter, the word for marking which letter swaps out

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A circus clown is given a pet animal in exchange for some money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting a pet for pounds' swaps the L in CLOWN for A PET.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African city is the country's legislative seat, one of its three capitals.

clue.text: Primate trapped in escape manoeuvre

indicators.note: the letters are trapped inside the words escape manoeuvre, across the gap

explanation.surface: A monkey caught in the middle of a breakout attempt from a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' signals the answer within 'escAPE MANoeuvre'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a creature imagined as half human and half great ape, a kind of primate.

clue.text: Opponent of privilege revising inter alia a guidebook at the start

indicators.note: revising the text rewrites its letters in a different arrangement
at the start of the word guidebook comes its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone against privilege rewrites a guidebook's opening, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revising' signals an anagram of INTER ALIA, A and G ('guidebook at the start').
explanation.definitionFit: A believer in equal rights for all people naturally opposes special privilege.

clue.text: Part of world Eco's written about with enthusiasm at first ignored

indicators.note: written about means written the other way round, so the name Eco is turned back
the opening letter of the word for enthusiasm is ignored

parts.note: a mania is a craze or enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Umberto Eco is written about eagerly, though at first ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns ECO into OCE; 'at first ignored' drops the M of MANIA, giving ANIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific islands with Australia form a region, one of the world's geographic divisions.

clue.text: Require massage, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word said out loud that is spelt differently

parts.note: to knead muscles is to massage them

explanation.surface: Someone saying they need a massage, by the sound of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Linette's new name

indicators.note: a new version of the name Linette is its letters put in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Linette has acquired a new name, perhaps through marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' signals an anagram of LINETTE; the 's is read as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a book or film its title is to call it something, so the verb works as a synonym.

clue.text: How rent under lease is paid, exact in every way

definitions.text: How rent under lease is paid
definitions.meaning: a tenant pays rent to the landlord, the one who lets the property

explanation.surface: How rent under a lease is paid: precisely, in every detail.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is a pun: a 'letter' is someone who lets property, so rent goes to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means following instructions with complete precision, every detail observed.

clue.text: Clever securing English tree

indicators.note: one word securing another holds it fast within itself

explanation.surface: A clever gardener manages to secure an English tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is another name for the white poplar, a crossword-familiar tree.

clue.text: Feature of writing unit act upon at work

indicators.note: letters at work are busy rearranging themselves into something new

explanation.surface: An instruction to a military unit to act upon some feature of a written order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' signals an anagram of UNIT ACT UPON.
explanation.definitionFit: Commas, full stops and the like are a defining feature of written text, absent from speech.

clue.text: One going over shortcoming, bore at heart

parts.note: a defect is a flaw or shortcoming

indicators.note: the heart of the word bore is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A dull person crossing over, whose failing is being a bore at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One going over' sounds like a reviewer, but means someone switching sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes over to the enemy side has deserted their own country or cause.

clue.text: Person displaying bathroom fixture

definitions.meaning: someone who shows or exhibits something, the agent noun of the verb show
a cubicle or spray head for washing under running water

explanation.surface: A showroom salesperson demonstrates a bathroom fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the rare agent noun 'one who shows', which reads differently from the washing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: One who shows things is literally a 'show-er'; the washing spray is the everyday sense.

clue.text: Torment journalists after work

indicators.note: the journalists come after the work in the answer

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: Journalists torment someone after work, hounding them home.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment a people is to subject them to harsh, unjust treatment, as a tyrant does.

clue.text: Residence of royal friend, superb

explanation.surface: A royal's home, as described by an admiring friend, is superb.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand official home of a monarch is the classic royal residence, such as Buckingham.

clue.text: Show disapproval of US soldier over Eastern dance

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: Jeering at an American soldier over a dance from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places BOOGI above E in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dance energetically to pop music is to boogie, informally.

clue.text: After training, pointer made to prevail

indicators.note: after training, the words pointer made are drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: A gundog, once trained, is made to win out at a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After training' signals an anagram of POINTER MADE; a pointer is a gundog.
explanation.definitionFit: To be the main or ruling element is to prevail over others, a close synonym.

clue.text: A British poem — "Home"

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A British poem titled 'Home'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling place where someone lives is their home, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Rise initially spoken of as ridiculous

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A price rise talked about as absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'spoken of as ridiculous'.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb high into the air, as a bird or kite does, is to rise.

clue.text: Manifest finished before time

indicators.note: one piece placed before the next in the answer

parts.note: when something is finished it is over
T is the abbreviation for time in physics

explanation.surface: A shipping manifest was finished ahead of the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manifest' looks like a noun (a cargo list) but is the adjective meaning plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something manifest is open and evident, not hidden, which is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: New order to bang out for patrol vessel

indicators.note: a new order of the words bang out means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A fresh command goes out to fire the guns aboard a patrol ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New order' signals an anagram of BANG OUT; 'to' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A small armed ship used to patrol rivers and coasts is exactly this kind of vessel.

clue.text: Booked, saying little

definitions.meaning: a table or seat that is booked has been held in advance
a quiet, reticent person keeps to themselves

explanation.surface: Someone booked in but keeping quiet about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from holding something back: a seat kept for someone, or feelings kept in.

clue.text: Be informed boss has right to replace daughter

indicators.note: one letter comes in to replace another, swapping the daughter out of the word for boss

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A family firm: the boss gives his right-hand man his daughter's job, and is told about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has right to replace daughter' swaps the D in HEAD for R.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn news from someone is to be told it, as in 'I hear you're moving'.
